newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland says safety of hostages comes first in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Poland says safety of hostages comes first in Peru.

text.p: Poland, whose charge d'affaires is among hostages held by armed guerrillas at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, said on Wednesday that the health and well-being of the captives was the top priority.
"We have set up a group within the foreign ministry to monitor the situation," the ministry's spokesman Pawel Dobrowolski said, adding that it had contacted Peruvian authorities.

Asked whether Poland had made any recommendations to Peru, he replied: "The obvious one that from our point of view the health and well-being of all the hostages, including the Polish charge d'affaires, is of paramount importance."
"Of course this has been accepted," he told Reuters.
Dobrowolski said military force was always a last resort in such situations and Poland did not have to suggest this to Peru as it had been understood from the beginning.
"We believe the only way is try to negotiate the whole situation out, but of course the final decisions, as always, rest with the countries that are most involved, Japan and Peru," Dobrowolski added.

He said the charge, Wojciech Tomaszewski, was the only Pole among hostages seized when guerrillas from the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) attacked the residence late on Tuesday during a reception.
The guerrillas have threatened to kill the hostages, including senior foreign diplomats, unless the government frees their jailed comrades.
Peru's President Alberto Fujimori put the number of hostages at 200 in a telephone conversation with Japan's Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
